gloss: to have trouble; to quarrel; to dispute

definitions.gloss: to have trouble; to quarrel; to dispute; to have a conflict
definitions.explanation: For people or parties to have disagreements or conflicts. Often used for disputes over money, inheritance, or interpersonal conflicts.

examples.japanese: {遺産|いさん}のことで{兄弟|きょうだい}が{揉|も}めている。
examples.english: The siblings are fighting over the inheritance.

examples.japanese: {近所|きんじょ}と{騒音|そうおん}のことで{揉|も}めた。
examples.english: We had a dispute with the neighbors over noise.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}と{揉|も}めずに{円満|えんまん}{退社|たいしゃ}したい。
examples.english: I want to leave the company amicably without any conflict.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY:
Intransitive verb ({自動詞|じどうし}). Related transitive form: {揉|も}む (to massage; to rub).

USAGE:
{揉|も}める specifically refers to interpersonal or inter-party conflicts and disputes. Common contexts include:
・お{金|かね}で{揉|も}める - to fight over money
・{遺産|いさん}で{揉|も}める - to dispute over inheritance
・{離婚|りこん}で{揉|も}める - to have conflicts during divorce

COMMON PATTERNS:
・〜と{揉|も}める (to have a dispute with ~)
・〜のことで{揉|も}める (to fight over ~)
・{揉|も}め{事|ごと} (trouble, dispute - noun form)

RELATED WORDS:
・{揉|も}め{事|ごと} - trouble, dispute
・{揉|も}め{合|あ}う - to struggle/scuffle together

REGISTER:
Casual to neutral. Common in everyday conversation.
